analysis.investment_thesis: Gillette India is an exceptional business — ROCE of 58.78%, zero debt, and consistent FCF — but the Magic Formula demands BOTH quality AND cheapness; at an earnings yield of ~2.2% (EBIT INR 571 Cr / EV ~INR 25,398 Cr), it fails the cheapness test catastrophically. A great company at a terrible price is still a terrible investment.
key_strengths: Exceptional return on capital: ROCE 58.78% sustained over multiple years — a genuinely rare, durable business
Asset-light, cash-generative: FCF INR 442 Cr on capex of just INR 67 Cr (87% OCF conversion)
Zero debt, INR 473 Cr net cash — fortress balance sheet with no financial risk
key_risks: Earnings yield ~2.2% (EBIT/EV) is one-seventh of our 15% threshold — market price embeds decades of perfection
Revenue CAGR of 9.4% is modest for a stock trading at 48x earnings — growth must accelerate sharply to justify valuation
75% promoter (P&G) ownership caps free-float and creates governance concentration risk
red_flags: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) of ~2.2% is far below the 6% floor where the Magic Formula even considers a stock
P/E of 48x and EV/EBITDA of 28x price in flawless execution for 15+ years with no margin for error
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT ≈ INR 571 Cr (operating income 2024); Enterprise Value = INR 25,871 Cr market cap minus INR 473 Cr cash = ~INR 25,398 Cr. Earnings Yield = 571/25,398 = **2.2%** — a disaster by our criteria where anything below 6% is overvalued and anything above 15% is attractive. ROCE at 58.78% is world-class and the business earns it honestly: gross margins of 63%, operating margins of 29%, and capex of just INR 67 Cr against INR 509 Cr of operating cash flow. This is exactly the kind of business the Magic Formula loves to own — when it's cheap.

The problem is price. At 48x earnings with 9.4% revenue CAGR, an investor pays a massive premium for a business growing at single-digit rates. FCF yield to market cap is a mere 1.7% (INR 442 Cr / INR 25,871 Cr). The Magic Formula ranks stocks on BOTH earnings yield AND ROIC; Gillette India would rank in the top decile on ROIC but bottom decile on earnings yield — disqualifying it from the combined ranking entirely. This is a stock to watch at half the price (implied ~24x P/E, earnings yield ~4-5%), not to buy today.
